It has also trained scientists in high-field magnets, tritium handling, and remote maintenance, strengthening nuclear safety and industrial precision. Materials developed for fusion reactors, such as low-activation steels and silicon carbide composites, improve aerospace, automotive, and energy-storage components. Superconducting magnet programs for fusion advanced MRI, NMR, and grid-scale storage technologies, while neutron irradiation studies help make medical isotopes and harden electronics. Its iritic value is visible in medical, energy, and manufacturing spinoffs.
